implementerProof.how: Both halves re-measured here rather than read. The flakiness my round 9 failed on is gone under the same loader that produced it: five runs of cluster.test.sh, one after another, each under four busy loops on this 3-CPU pod, all 52 PASS and 0 FAIL (round 9: two of two runs red, on `the bundle streamed into the runner did not go through runner_exec` and `the heartbeat of a held run patched the lock no more than before`). The loader and the runs were one named harness job, loadloop-infra-598, so the whole thing had a real pid, which is the handle `$!` never gave me in this shell. I also read the two changes rather than trusting their titles: guarded_by_lock_read now pairs a write with the lock read of the same SESSION, taken from field 4 of /proc/<pid>/stat and written per call into a new one-line-per-call kubectl-calls.log, so a daemon (each setsid, so a session of its own) calling kubectl in between no longer breaks the pairing, and a call whose arguments span lines no longer does either; the held-heartbeat check now waits for three more lock patches, with 300 s as a hang's backstop, instead of `sleep 1` and a single patch. Neither is weaker: the first still demands the write be its command's next kubectl call after the read, the second now demands three cycles where it demanded one.

proof.criterion: The two test changes do not weaken what they assert
proof.surface: the suite's own source, and a control copy of cluster.sh with one lock read removed
proof.command: git diff 32592e51 183c0d7f -- packages/envoy/loadtest/cluster/cluster.test.sh; then a scratch copy of the loadtest tree whose postgres_exec skips copy_is_ours for pg_restore alone (`case "$*" in pg_restore*) : ;; *) copy_is_ours … ;; esac`) and bash loadtest/cluster/cluster.test.sh over it
proof.observed: The control fails exactly where it should and nowhere else: after 16 PASS, `FAIL: the pg_restore of the seed dump did not go through postgres_exec: no lock read came right before it (567:…exec postgres-0 -c postgres -- pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges -j 8 …)`, exit 1. So the session-paired assertion still catches a guarded write whose lock read is gone - it was the pairing that changed, not the demand. Reading the diff: the pairing is by the caller's session id and the new kubectl-calls.log holds one line per call (arguments with newlines escaped, truncated to 1,000 characters to stay one atomic write); the held-heartbeat count is by three patch events with a 300 s backstop
proof.negativeControl: The control itself is the negative control, and it is a mutation of the product rather than of the test: the only change is that one write loses its guard, and the suite notices

Main's race flake that I named at 00:30Z is gone from this head's lanes.

A measurement for the tree, from the pledge I made when the named-job sampler rule came in: a named harness job does give a real pid where `$!` gives nothing, and `proc://<name>/kill` stops the job - but it did not reap the job's in-flight grandchild. After the kill returned `Stopped loadloop-infra-598 — exited`, `timeout 2400 bash loadtest/cluster/cluster.test.sh` and its bash were still running, and I ended them by exact pid. So the rule's `jobs -l`-and-ps check before ending a turn matters for a named job too: kill the job, then look for what it left.

No cluster run and no namespace this round: the lock ConfigMap was absent throughout, nothing of mine touched the loadtest namespace, and the only load on the driving pod was my own loader, which is the measurement rather than a contaminant - there was no live pass to contaminate.
